findings.title: Unconditional extra backing-store lookup added to remove()
findings.body: In remove(), `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now called unconditionally before the isInvalid(cacheKey) check. Previously, when the cache entry was valid (`isInvalid(cacheKey)==false`), the method only consulted the local cache (`realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, ...)`) and never hit the delegate/JPA store in that branch. Now every remove() call performs an extra delegate lookup even when the cached CachedIdentityProvider already holds the needed model (available via `cached.getIdentityProvider()` in the else branch), adding an avoidable database round-trip to every IDP removal.

findings.title: Inconsistent wrapped vs raw model comparison in login-cache invalidation on update
findings.body: In update(), `idpById = getById(model.getInternalId())` returns an organization-aware wrapped IdentityProviderModel whose isEnabled() also factors in the linked organization's enabled state (see createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel), while `model` (the second argument passed straight through to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) is the raw, unwrapped model from the caller whose isEnabled() reflects only the stored 'enabled' attribute. Because getLoginPredicate() tests ENABLED via isEnabled(), comparing the wrapped 'original' against the raw 'updated' is inconsistent: when the organization is disabled, idpById.isEnabled() can be false even though the stored attribute is true, causing registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate to conclude 'no login-eligibility change' and skip cache invalidation even though the raw 'enabled' attribute genuinely changed. Since the underlying idpDelegate.getForLogin() query filters by the raw stored attribute (not the wrapped value), the cached ID list for getForLogin can become stale and keep referencing an IDP whose real enabled flag changed, violating the documented getForLogin() contract that only enabled/eligible IDPs are returned for callers that don't re-check isEnabled() themselves.

findings.title: No test covers organization enable/disable or removal affecting the new getForLogin cache
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin only exercises create/update/remove on the IdentityProvider itself to verify cache invalidation of the new getForLogin caches. It never tests disabling/enabling the linked Organization or removing the Organization entirely. This matters because OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java was specifically changed in this PR to re-check idp.isEnabled() at render time precisely because toggling an organization's enabled flag does not invalidate the getForLogin ID-list cache. There is no test verifying that disabling an organization correctly excludes its IDPs from login, nor that removing an organization properly invalidates/cleans up the new login caches for its linked IDPs, leaving this behavior unverified.

findings.title: Login-eligibility logic duplicated between getForLogin() search options and getLoginPredicate()
findings.body: The default getForLogin() method (lines 165-184) determines login eligibility by building search-option maps (LoginFilter.getLoginSearchOptions() plus explicit ORGANIZATION_ID/BROKER_PUBLIC handling), while the new getLoginPredicate() (lines 252-256) re-implements the same eligibility rules as a Predicate for use purely in cache-invalidation decisions in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider. These two independent representations of the same business rule must be kept manually in sync; if either is changed in the future without updating the other, the Infinispan cache invalidation logic will silently diverge from the actual query semantics, resulting in stale or incorrect getForLogin() cache results.
